office: I should probably focus. Right after this dramatic pause.
This office smells like dust, secrets, and coffee that lost its will to live.
A private detective's greatest weapon is observation. The second greatest is a receipt for expenses.
I should look busy. In this business, looking busy is half the investigation.
Somewhere out there, a criminal is making a mistake. Ideally one involving paperwork.
lab: Nothing says justice like fluorescent lighting.
If this machine explodes, I am blaming science.

lockedDrawer: Locked. Which is rude, but informative.
desk: A desk. The natural habitat of unpaid invoices.
Nothing suspicious here. Which is, frankly, suspicious.
Three drawers. All of them judging me.
The desk is clean. That is either professionalism or an alibi.
A warrant board, three cold coffees, and no assistant. The detective lifestyle.
globe: A globe. Proof that trouble can be geographically ambitious.
So many cities. So little budget for taxis.
Spin the globe, pick a city, ruin a criminal's afternoon.
fakePainting: A fake. And not even an ambitious one.
crimeBoard: The crime board: string, pins, and the fragile illusion that I know what I am doing.
Every clue has a place. Usually directly under another clue I forgot to read.
The board is ready. Now I only need facts, motive, opportunity, and several miracles.
caseFileCabinet: Case files: the place where every mystery begins with too much paperwork.
Some detectives trust instinct. I trust folders labelled 'URGENT'.
A filing cabinet. The natural predator of forgotten leads.
notesBook: My notes. Written in a code known only to me and future forensic linguists.
If I cannot read my own handwriting, neither can the criminals.
A good detective keeps notes. A great detective remembers where they put them.
wantedDatabase: Wanted suspects. Mostly terrible people with surprisingly good cheekbones.
A database full of faces. One of them is probably about to make my day worse.
Criminal records: social media, but with more warrants.
recoveredArtifacts: Recovered artefacts. History has a habit of getting stolen by people with poor taste.
Every artefact has survived centuries. Then someone tried to sell it online.
A shelf of treasures, each with a story and an insurance claim.
atlas: An atlas. Because criminals insist on fleeing somewhere picturesque.
Maps never show the queues, the jet lag, or the suspiciously expensive airport sandwiches.
The world is large. Fortunately, criminals are fond of leaving clues.
brokenElevator: Out of order. A bold career choice for an elevator.
The elevator is dead. It had a good run. Mostly between floors.
A sign says 'Out of Order.' At least someone here is being honest.
